structural: The text for `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.Yaml` prescribes a unit struct `pub struct Yaml;`. It also prescribes trait implementations of `Clone`, `Debug`, `Default`, `Copy` and `OutlineLang`. The extension, selection and fingerprint rules are behavioral and are described elsewhere in the chapter.

The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs#macro@724fb0b38030` is the invocation `language!(Yaml, yaml::PROFILE)`. It carries the `{impl}` markers.

I read the `language!` macro definition, `macro[language]` in the same file. For the name it receives, it expands to `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)] pub struct $name;`. It also expands to `impl super::OutlineLang for $name`, which has `name`, `extensions`, `outline`, `fingerprint_scheme` and `search_structure` methods that read from the profile.

The invocation therefore produces the public unit struct `Yaml` with all five required trait implementations. The macro definition is reached from the marked invocation, so it needs no separate marker.

The profile `yaml::PROFILE` supplies the language-specific rules. Those are behavioral obligations and belong to other requirements.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.Yaml` declares the `Yaml` unit struct and its trait implementations (`Clone`, `Debug`, `Default`, `OutlineLang`, `Copy`). It also says `Yaml` supplies the extension, selection and fingerprint rules described in the chapter. Those detailed rules belong to the refining requirements `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.language`, `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items` and `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints`, so they are not reassessed here.

The tests cover the observable obligations that remain:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` runs the generic helper `check` on `languages::Yaml`. The helper's bounds `OutlineLang + Default + Copy` require those traits at compile time. It asserts `extensions()` equals `["yml","yaml"]` and `fingerprint_scheme()` equals `yaml-structural-v1`. It asserts that `size_of` is 0, that `Clone::clone` preserves the extensions, and that `Yaml::default()` has the same fingerprint scheme.
- The same helper builds the outline from `a.YAML` and checks `pair[check]` is selectable and the root span covers the source. It also checks that `.YML` and `.YAML` names are inferred case-insensitively, that `from_source_with` works with the explicit language, and that `search_structure` returns valid ranges.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry]` checks the YAML selection behavior through the `Yaml` implementation. It covers trailing comments, comments before sequence items, and comments before the next pair. It also checks nested pairs and span consistency.

`Debug` has no stated behavior beyond the trait implementation, which is a structural or compile-time matter. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs` checks the public export inventory, and that covers the declared item. I found no behavioral gap.
